## Natural history notes

A small geometrid moth characterized by mottled gray to brownish wings with fine wavy lines and bark-like shading that helps it blend into tree trunks, dead leaves, and woody stems. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on woody plant foliage and contribute to the broader food web as prey for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
